analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md and the supplied change map/patch against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. The visible change admits variable-frame-rate GLM video and assigns frame times by index/nominalFrameRate rather than refusing it (patch at BASE 810–811 and 827). This broadens adversarial media input but does not itself demonstrate a vulnerability. BASE 812–826 documents decoded-byte, prepared-pixel and reservation limits; BASE 828–833 excludes media from prefix reuse and speculation. Integration should verify that the changed GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset implementation preserves bounded decoding and that GLM5NextVisionBudget.videoTokenCeiling remains conservative for indexed variable-rate tracks, including inconsistent rate/duration metadata. These contracts affect A-001 and TB-007 availability and media isolation; implementation evidence is absent here.
Also examined unchanged context for tokenizer/template qualification (847–879), calibration and retirement ownership (934–1070), ingress audio authorization (1074–1085), cache scoping and donor/billing attribution (1108–1170), deadline admission (1280–1437), and MTP replacement/output bounds (1451–1608). No supplied change establishes a regression in encryption, serving authorization, billing or T-041 account isolation. Additional HEAD text at 876–880 is listed in the complete change map but its contents are not supplied; BASE template requirements cannot establish what that addition changes. Integration must examine that addition and corresponding changed tokenizer qualification code, if any. This documentation-only evidence supports no concrete finding and does not establish runtime safety.
